oil.summary: Crude markets sold off sharply today, with WTI collapsing 6.39% to $89.66/bbl and RBOB cratering 7.85% to $3.1976/gal, even as the geopolitical backdrop remains acutely supportive. The Saudi East-West pipeline restart—the kingdom's main Red Sea bypass route at up to 4 mb/d—appears to have triggered the selloff, offering the market at least a partial supply relief valve. However, countervailing pressures remain intense: Iran's declared oil blockade on Gulf neighbors continues, Strait of Hormuz flows hit a six-month high as the U.S.-Iran conflict grinds on, and VLCC freight costs are reportedly exploding on trapped tonnage. The newly signed Russia-Iran sanctions bill adds further complexity, with Washington simultaneously easing some Russia sanctions via a temporary deal to cap prices. India's Russian crude imports fell 16.5% in August, redirecting flows. The WTI-Brent spread widened notably, with Brent's 1.89% decline far more modest than WTI's drop, reflecting differential supply dynamics.
drivers: Saudi East-West pipeline restart restores partial Red Sea bypass capacity, triggering sharp near-term supply relief and selling pressure
Iran's Hormuz blockade of Gulf neighbors persists even as Iranian own exports flow through the strait; U.S.-Iran war continues with Trump threatening escalation
Contradictory U.S. sanctions posture—new Russia-Iran bill signed while a temporary Russia sanctions ease is enacted—creates policy uncertainty across supply chains

gas.summary: Henry Hub surged 11.88% on the day to $3.173/MMBtu, extending a strong monthly gain of 14.42% and a weekly gain of 8.70%, signaling tightening U.S. gas balances. European TTF was comparatively quiet, edging up just 0.85% to €73.875/MWh, though it remains elevated on a monthly basis (+12.16%). On the demand destruction side, INEOS confirmed it is idling three UK chemical plants citing uncompetitive European gas prices—a direct signal of industrial load shedding. A new armed group blockade at Libya's Sharara oilfield, cutting pipeline flows to its largest crude producing site, adds incremental associated-gas supply risk to an already tight market. News flow on gas-specific fundamentals was otherwise thin today.
drivers: Henry Hub jumped nearly 12% intraday, sustaining a robust monthly uptrend driven by tightening U.S. supply-demand balances
INEOS idling three UK chemical plants on high European gas prices signals industrial demand destruction at current TTF levels
Armed blockade at Libya's Sharara oilfield threatens associated gas output and adds further regional supply disruption risk

power.summary: EU Carbon EUAs were essentially flat on the day at $82.44/EUA (-0.12%), holding near one-month highs (+5.58% over 30 days), broadly tracking the elevated TTF gas complex. A headline piece flagged utility profit margins as an emerging political target, with rising electricity prices, fuel costs, and capital expenditures squeezing the sector from multiple directions simultaneously. Europe's offshore wind supply chain faces its own headwinds, with monopile manufacturers shifting from capacity constraints to weak factory utilization as offshore order flow softens. A longer-dated demand signal came from a report projecting global energy demand to rise 60% by 2060, led by emerging economies. News flow in power and carbon was relatively thin today; EUA price action was muted and appeared to lack a fresh catalyst.
drivers: EU Carbon EUAs flat on the day but holding monthly gains, with elevated TTF providing a cost-of-generation floor that keeps carbon pricing supported
European offshore wind monopile manufacturers moving into underutilization, signaling a slowdown in renewable capacity build-out that could pressure long-term clean power supply
Rising electricity prices drawing political scrutiny of utility profits, adding regulatory risk to power sector capex and operating outlooks
